_comment: Phase 4.2, the house's matches (MatchSystem). The heir asks for someone's hand face to face, or accepts a suitor sent by a neighbouring noble house; kin and retainers can be matched from their card. A proposal is weighed, never rolled: everyone answers yes or no and says why, like an offer of service (data/recruitment.json).

ages._comment: Who can be matched: grown, of an age with each other.

consent._comment: score = base + the parts below; they say yes at threshold. opinion_* are per point of opinion (-100..100). station: marrying into a higher station (into the house, or into a retainer's family). duty: the house's own kin do as the house asks (unless they dislike the match or love another). loyalty (retainers) is per point above loyalty_from: the loyal accept a stranger, the rest must like them. A gap in age beyond gap_from costs gap_cost a year. Traits add their value.

answers._comment: What they say. {lord} = my lord / my lady.
yes: I'd hoped you would ask. Yes!
yes_duty: If it pleases the house, then yes.
I'll do my duty by the house. Yes.
no: No. Please don't ask me again.
no_partner: I won't marry {name}. Not even for the house.
Ask anything else of me, but not that.

wedding._comment: What a wedding does for the house: renown (a noble match raises it, marrying beneath the house a little lowers it), the village's opinion of the heir when the heir marries one of their own, and the spouse's opinion and loyalty.

suitors._comment: Neighbouring houses offer a son or daughter for the house's unmarried (the heir first). The suitor visits for visit_days, staying at the manor, so you can meet them and look at them with the Eye; accept or decline before they leave. One visit at a time. yearly_*: how many offers come a year, on average (the next is due 0.5 to 1.5 times the average gap after the last visit ends). The dowry (gold) grows with their house's renown.

meeting._comment: What a suitor says when the heir first speaks with them: "heir" when they came for the heir, "kin" when for one of the house. {seat}: their home; {name}: whom they came for; {lord}: my lord / my lady.
heir: I've ridden from {seat} to meet you, {lord}. I hope I don't disappoint.
So you're the one my family wrote of. Good day, {lord}.
{seat} sends its greetings, {lord}. I bring my own as well.
kin: I've come from {seat} to meet {name}. Will you speak well of me, {lord}?
My family hopes I'll marry {name}. I hope so too, {lord}.

houses._comment: The noble houses around the village (RealmData): how many, and their renown.

praise._comment: What a suitor's family writes of them: always glowing, a clue to their true gift at best (the family boasts; only the Eye tells the truth). By attribute, then how impressive it sounds (mild, keen, striking). {He}/{he}/{his} follow the suitor.
leadership: {He} is well liked by the whole household.
{He} is already trusted with the steward's men.
{He} sits naturally at the head of the table.
{He} was born to command, all who know {him} say.
combat: {He} is a fair rider and fond of the hunt.
{He} is the best hand with a sword among the young of our house.
{He} unhorsed a knight at the spring tourney.
{He} has never been beaten at arms.
{He} is spoken of as a champion in the making.
intelligence: {He} has a rare head for figures.
{He} is wiser than {his} years by far.
politics: {He} has a gentle way with guests.
{He} is at ease among the great of the land.
{He} could charm a bishop out of his ring.
administration: {He} is careful with the household's coin.
{He} keeps our accounts better than our steward.
{He} has a firm hand on the storerooms.
Not a penny is ever lost in {his} keeping.
ambition: {He} means to rise high, and will.
{He} will make your house greater than it was.
{He} dreams of a seat at the king's own table.
